RL Training Report

Generated from metrics logs

Training Health

PPO Metrics

Tracks the PPO optimizer health during training. Policy Loss should decrease and stabilize (not diverge to -/+ infinity). Value Loss measures how well the value function predicts returns — it typically decreases then plateaus. Entropy (negated) shows exploration: higher values mean the agent is exploring more actions; a sharp drop means the policy is collapsing. KL Divergence and Clip Fraction indicate how large the PPO policy updates are — a KL spike means the policy changed too fast.

Win Rates

Overall Win Rate

Rolling win rate across all opponents. The red dashed line marks 50% (random play). A well-trained model should trend above 50% over time.

Per-Opponent Win Rate

Rolling win rate for each opponent separately, plotted by episode index. Lines are interleaved because the trainer rotates between opponents. A line above 50% means the agent beats that opponent more often than not.

Per-Opponent Heatmap

Win rate per opponent broken into 10 training phases (equal step intervals). Green = high win rate, red = low win rate. Useful for spotting when the agent learns or forgets a matchup.

No data for: Evaluation Matrix

Game Statistics

Finish Reason Distribution

How games ended — by win (green) and loss (red). 'prize_cards' = taking all 6 prizes; 'deck_out' = opponent (or you) ran out of cards; 'no_pokemon' = opponent had no Pokemon left; 'step_limit' = hit the max turn limit.

Turn Count Distribution

Histogram of game lengths (in turns) for wins vs losses. Longer games suggest control/slow strategies; shorter games suggest aggressive/fast wins or quick losses.

Invalid Action Rate

Fraction of agent actions that were illegal and had to be retried. Should trend toward zero as the agent learns which actions are legal. A flat non-zero rate means the agent repeatedly tries illegal moves.

Strategy

Action Frequency Over Time

Proportion of each action type (attack, attach energy, play card, evolve, retreat, use ability, end turn) across training. Changes in proportions show how the agent's strategy evolves — e.g. more attacks and fewer 'end turns' as it learns.

Reward Component Breakdown

Average contribution of each reward signal per episode over training. The black line at y=0 separates positive rewards (above) from penalties (below). 'win' = terminal +1/-1 for win/loss; 'prizes' = prize card differential; 'damage' = HP dealt vs taken; 'turn_penalty' = -0.01 per turn (discourages idle play); 'ko' = knockout bonus; 'domain' = game-strategy penalties (Ignition Energy waste, double energy, pass penalty, deck-out penalty, etc.). Watch for 'domain' trending upward — it means the agent is learning to avoid common mistakes.

Win Rate by Proton Usage

Win rate grouped by how Team Rocket's Proton was used. 'Proton Turn 1-2' = used Proton early (ideal); 'Proton Turn 3+' = used Proton late; 'No Proton' = never used it. The 'n=' label shows how many games fell into each category.

Advanced

Energy Attachment Heatmap

Average energy count on your active Pokemon per turn, broken down by Pokemon. Darker colors = more energy attached. Useful for seeing energy ramp-up patterns and whether the agent attaches energy consistently or hoards them.

Opening Hand Win Rate

Win rate conditioned on what was in the agent's opening hand. Each bar shows whether having that card (e.g. 'has_Proton') correlates with a higher or lower win rate. The red dashed line marks 50%. 'n=' shows sample size.

No data for: Card Co-occurrence

Prize Tempo

Average prizes remaining at game end, plotted by total game length. Your prizes (blue) vs opponent prizes (red) — the gap indicates how dominant the win/loss was. A wide gap at low turn count means fast, decisive games.
